name: Adisoft Technologies Limited
summary: Adisoft is an industrial-automation integrator, not a recurring-revenue software company. Its engineering relationships, growth and profitable project delivery are meaningful, but concentrated customers, weak cumulative cash conversion and a large new factory make the investment less straightforward than reported ROCE or a roughly 21 x earnings multiple suggests. This completed deep assessment is a watchlist/special-situation review, not a buy conclusion. BQS5.40 and Growth Quality raw 6.55, capped at 5.00 for persistently weak cash realization. The linked base illustration returns 7.91% annually versus a 15% hurdle; a severe collection/customer-loss stress is unfunded without further financing. IAS remains NS under the financial-reliability hold: cash-flow line classifications, interest/tax presentation and confirmations require an authoritative bridge. This is not a fraud or actual-default finding. The recent preliminary sales update improves demand visibility, not proof of cash collection or completed factory economics. Model corrected on 20 October 2026 for opening obligations and retained terminal claims; historical financial figures are unchanged.

sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text:
Adisoft is an industrial-automation integrator, not a recurring-revenue software company. Its engineering relationships, growth and profitable project delivery are meaningful, but concentrated customers, weak cumulative cash conversion and a large new factory make the investment less straightforward than reported ROCE or a roughly 21 x earnings multiple suggests. This completed deep assessment is a watchlist/special-situation review, not a buy conclusion. BQS5.40 and Growth Quality raw 6.55, capped at 5.00 for persistently weak cash realization. The linked base illustration returns 7.91% annually versus a 15% hurdle; a severe collection/customer-loss stress is unfunded without further financing. IAS remains NS under the financial-reliability hold: cash-flow line classifications, interest/tax presentation and confirmations require an authoritative bridge. This is not a fraud or actual-default finding. The recent preliminary sales update improves demand visibility, not proof of cash collection or completed factory economics.

Model correction dated20 October2026: opening obligations and terminal claims have been reconciled separately from new forecast expenses. Reported historical financial statements are unchanged. The corrected scenario values are in section10.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Confidence
sections.text: Adisoft Technologies Limited, NSE Emerge ADISOFT, ISIN INE20PL01012; listed April 30,2026. Cutoff October 20,2026. Indian GAAP Accounting Standards consolidated accounts include a 24% AIOI associate through equity-method profit, not full associate revenue. The official October 19 close ₹293,16318000 shares and 800-share lot imply ₹478.1174 crore equity value and ₹234400 minimum lot value. Horizon five years; assumed nominal equity hurdle 15% before investor tax, not WACC or a personalized allocation. G1 conditional, with historical compliance failures and control weaknesses but no substantiated diversion. G2 hold for the material cash-flow/confirmation bridge, despite unmodified audit and IFC opinions. G3 conditional: IPO funds support the selected base, but severe stress needs additional funding. G4 conditional: current ESM-I/ST/5% band and lot size matter despite good observed turnover. Identity/quote confidence High; historical figures, governance and explicit stress inputs Medium; precision of normalized CFO Low. Forecast uncertainty is High even where verified starting inputs support Medium evidence confidence.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: Canonical factors GOV4,MOAT6,REV8,DUR6,CAP7,CASH2,BAL5,EXEC5,EARN6. BQS weighted contributions .80+1.20+.96+.60+.84+.20+.40+.40=5.40. Growth Quality contributions 3.20+1.20+.90+1.05+.20=6.55, capped at 5 because the weak multi-year CASH2 result is persistent. IAS inputs Q5.40,R2,D2,P4,L6 imply an illustrative raw 3.45; G2 makes the final IAS NS and excludes all investable rankings. No missing-factor reweighting or substituted neutral scores. REV uses the three-year same-operating-business bridge, with other operating revenue regrouped consistently; Medium confidence/history ceiling limits the ≥30% starting score 9 to 8. R2 corresponds to 7.91% modeled return minus 15%=−7.04 percentage points. Factor records preserve contrary facts and source-linked reasoning.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: Adisoft designs, procures, assembles, tests and commissions automated assembly lines, material-handling systems, robotic cells, machine-vision inspection, traceability and shop-floor/IT integration. Clients buy production reliability and process control, not a disclosed annual software subscription. FY2026 revenue ₹166.42 crore includes automation domestic ₹112.81,export ₹2.95,services ₹13.50 and automation-parts trading ₹37.16; FY2025 equivalents ₹73.74/3.97/19.72/32.91. Parts trading is 22.3% of sales and has lower margins in management commentary. Goods revenue is recognized when risks/control pass, described as leaving company premises; services follow contractual rendering. Dispatch, acceptance, retention and collection are therefore different milestones. Material purchases less inventory movement ₹111.37 crore leave ₹55.05 crore value added before employee/other costs, up from ₹39.71 crore on the annual comparative. The 24% AIOI investment contributes only ₹.13 crore associate profit in FY2026. Software references and reusable libraries do not establish a SaaS valuation.

sections.title: Moat and Industry Position
sections.text: Mechanism: integration knowledge, reusable engineering and customer-specific process familiarity can raise switching costs where production errors create expensive downtime. Evidence: multi-year OEM relationships, repeat deployments, increasing absolute operating profit and management-described cross-shop IT integration. Durability is moderate rather than structural: no independent market-share denominator or disclosed renewal/retention economics, and capable automation integrators can compete for new lines. Mitsubishi channel awards and ISO certification are execution/qualification signals, not exclusive distribution or guaranteed pricing power. The prospectus disclosed no firm long-term customer commitments and top-ten customer concentration 77.19/75.13/74.09% in FY2023/2024/2025; the largest supplied 38.88/50.86/48.48%. Seven-month October 2025 largest 43.39% and top-ten 70.18% are not a full-year diversification proof. Top-ten suppliers supplied 76.57% of FY2025 purchases and 81.07% in the stub, also without long-term supply contracts. Proprietary design/reuse can improve margins, but the prospectus still reported pending trademark registration. MOAT6 recognizes useful, contestable capability, not patents or monopoly inferred from awards.

sections.title: Revenue Growth and Scale
sections.text: Original standalone FY2022 revenue/PAT ₹39.3222/3.0991 crore and FY2023₹75.5073/6.1215 use the original report; the FY2024 report reclassifies its FY2023 revenue comparative to ₹75.1322. Final IPO-restated consolidated FY2023/2024/2025 revenue ₹75.5427/103.2685/131.7178 and PAT ₹6.0793/11.7557/16.1108 are retained separately. FY2026 annual revenue ₹166.42 includes ₹1.18 crore other operating revenue under other income; adding it for consistent comparison gives ₹167.60. Thus FY2023–FY2026 comparable revenue CAGR≈30.42%, annual additions ₹27.7258,₹28.4493,₹35.8822 crore. Without that regrouping the three-year endpoint CAGR≈30.12%; both map to the same capped REV8. Five-/ten-year comparable endpoints are unavailable, so no invented CAGR. FY2026 annual-comparative growth 27.68% is not spliced silently into the IPO series. Growth reflects increased automation work and mix, not full consolidation of AIOI; precise volume/pricing split is undisclosed. October 14 management reports preliminary H1FY2027 sales about ₹72 crore versus ₹48.96, roughly 47% growth. It supplies no reviewed H1 profit, balance sheet or CFO; do not annualize it or call it TTM audited growth. FY2026 H2₹117.46 crore supplied 70.6% of annual revenue, making seasonality material. Automotive share fell from 78.61% FY2025 to 64% FY2026 in management’s presentation, but remains a concentrated cycle exposure.

sections.title: Growth Quality and Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: The funded new Bhosari facility combines engineering, assembly, software and testing. The IPO budget totals ₹40.0087 crore, of which ₹2.2353 was already incurred and ₹37.7734 funded from IPO proceeds; March CWIP ₹2.47 crore is a separate audited balance and not automatically the same cutoff. Furniture/computing equipment form part of this budget, not a second factory. June monitoring records ₹1.04 crore capex deployed and ₹36.73 remaining. Management’s capacity claim of 4–5 x current revenue is not a demand forecast; October executable orders ₹50+ crore and pipeline≈₹40 crore must remain separate. Normal project cycles are three–four months, with limited disclosed cancellation/age/margin information. Bottom-up forecasts cap five-year growth well below the theoretical factory capacity and charge working capital, maintenance, new depreciation and full remaining project cash. Historical invested capital retaining deposits, equity+debt−true cash, rises ₹69.71→89.61 crore in FY2026. Conservative EBIT excluding all other income rises ₹19.54→29.69;25%-tax incremental return proxy 38.25%, or roughly 20.39% holding prior margin constant. Both exceed an explicitly assumed 13–17% nominal cost-of-capital range, but margin expansion on existing operations is not proof the new factory earns those returns. CAP7 therefore recognizes historical economics with a major unproven cohort. Cash conversion, not accounting ROCE, caps Growth Quality.

sections.title: Management, Governance and Execution
sections.text: The September 22 AGM record-date voting denominator verifies 12009950 promoter shares out of 16318000,73.5994%, and 1345 shareholders. It is not a September 30 shareholding or pledge-clearance filing. FY2026 director remuneration ₹.96 crore versus ₹1.024 crore previously; promoter loans ₹2.07 crore were repaid. Related AIOI purchases ₹4.28 crore and closing creditors ₹2.41 require commercial monitoring, but are not evidence of diversion. The prospectus candidly discloses historical Companies Act/ROC failures, including omitted cash-flow/consolidation filings and charges, with later consolidated statements approved September 22,2025 and compounding applications submitted. An application is not a verified final closure. Prior auditor S.D.Dale resigned June 1,2025 citing other assignments; KPNB appointed June 6, and a different peer reviewer restated the IPO accounts because of KPNB preoccupation. No dispute is inferred. FY2026 main and IFC opinions are unmodified, while the auditor states audit-trail functionality did not operate throughout and cannot comment on tampering; controls were being formalized. July correction explicitly fixes audited labels/XBRL and explains why March IPO certificates were inapplicable, since proceeds arrived in May. Factory promise tracking: June call partial operation September/October, August presentation November, October update end-Q3FY2027; full integration targeted March 2027. This is a modest slippage to monitor, not a claimed completed plant. No pending issuer/promoter litigation was disclosed in IPO categories; this is dated issuer disclosure, not universal legal clearance.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
FY2026 consolidated PBT ₹30.81 crore, PAT before associate ₹22.80 and total PAT ₹22.93 compare with annual FY2025₹21.49/15.95/16.12; the IPO restatement differs slightly and is separately reconciled for interest timing, warranty, actuarial benefits, tax and prepaid expenses. Other income ₹2.91 includes ₹1.62 interest,₹1.18 other operating revenue,₹.08 FX and ₹.03 drawback. Inventory is net ₹16.65 crore after ₹9.76 crore obsolescence provision; the ₹.17 crore reversal benefits current earnings. A bounded core PAT range ₹19.54–21.81 crore excludes interest/FX and inventory reversal, varies inclusion of other operating revenue and uses 25–30% tax, retaining ₹.13 associate earnings. No automatic add-back of all gratuity is made. Post-IPO16318000 shares reduce reported FY2026 economic EPS to ₹14.05 rather than pre-IPO weighted ₹19.09; normalized EPS≈₹11.98–13.37.

Reported CFO FY2023/2024/2025 IPO-restated ₹3.0318/−6.4132/−.7247 and FY2026₹17.34. Latest three years sum ₹10.2021 against PAT ₹50.7965,20.1% conversion; cash capex ₹.2231/.13/2.82 leaves ₹7.0290 before financing interest, about ₹3.08 after the disclosed finance-cost proxy. The original FY2022 CFO ₹6.3029 and capex ₹8.4710 are retained as standalone history, not omitted because the recent period is adverse. FY2026 receivables ₹82.47 versus ₹56.13 absorb ₹26.34 crore; payables ₹44.34 versus ₹27.17 provide ₹17.17 crore, so improved CFO partly relies on supplier credit. Closing receivables equal 181 sales-days; most are under six months, but this does not establish collection. June management says only ₹28–29 crore remained pending, without a reviewed subsequent balance.

The cash-flow page requires clarification, not a silent correction: it adds ₹6.93 crore on a taxes-paid-net-refund line, shows ₹.19 interest in CFO and−₹.19 investing versus ₹1.62 P&L interest, and includes provision/advance movements not directly reconcilable to balance-sheet deltas. Its cash definition includes ₹25.15 crore deposits over three months, up from ₹15.65; true cash falls ₹8.13→4.28 while all bank balances rise ₹23.78→29.43. Merely flipping tax signs would produce ₹3.48 crore CFO, but that is a mechanical sensitivity, not a corrected statement, because other tax/classification lines may offset. Total cash/debt/capex bridge supports meaningful cash generation, not a claim all CFO is fictitious. Note 40 leaves debtor/creditor/advance balances subject to confirmation/reconciliation; annual nil contingencies also needs a bridge to IPO-disclosed October 2025 bank guarantees ₹2.6014. These material unresolved links justify G2 hold without alleging fraud.

sections.title: Valuation and Linked Scenarios
sections.text:
At ₹293, equity value ₹478.1174 crore is 20.85 x reported post-IPO earnings, or roughly 21.92–24.47 x the economic PAT range. Enterprise value must distinguish pledged/earmarked deposits, IPO funds and subsequently repaid loans; no undated cash-adjusted multiple is presented as current. The five-year model starts from actual March operating WC ₹55.13 crore, cash ₹4.28, debt ₹21.55 and separate long deposits ₹25.15. It adds conservative net IPO ₹63.1035 once, incorporating the monitor-confirmed ₹1.29 expense saving reallocation and retaining≈₹.2441 issue-expense buffer. Debt repayment ₹12.39 includes ₹2.39 under GCP plus ₹10 allocated repayment reported by the board as used in Q2; this is a pro-forma bridge, not a verified October balance sheet. All long deposits are excluded from operating funding pending release evidence. Full IPO factory ₹37.7734 is paid once in year 1, including June spending;₹10 WC and ₹2.9 raw-material GCP are not deducted again beyond linked WC. Forecast incremental WC55% of positive sales change never overwrites opening balances or releases WC on contraction. Opening tax/statutory payment ₹6.0975 assumes 75% of ₹7.75 government balances offset ₹7.88 tax provision, plus ₹4.03 statutory dues;A zero-credit bound is now included; the reference remains conditional on the75% offset assumption, not a verified tax-credit split. Current employee provisions add ₹0.24 crore once and ₹1.24 crore noncurrent employee claims are retained at terminal.

Base growth 20/15/12/10/8%,18% EBITDA margin,₹1.5 first-year depreciation, followed by a ₹2.5 crore full-year base scaled with revenue,10% debt interest,25% tax,maintenance/growth capex and 15 x terminal NOPAT produce ₹428.74 terminal share value and 7.91% annual return, funded under assumptions. Bull 25/22/18/15/12%,20% margin and 18 x NOPAT gives ₹685.51/18.53%, also funded. Deposits receive 20% exit haircut and associate book value 20% haircut; no separate plant NAV is added to earnings value. Margin 15/18/20% by multiple 10/15/18 sensitivities accompany 12/15/18% hurdle-entry prices ₹243.28/213.16/187.41. These are analyst scenarios, not fair-price promises. No rescue financing or dilution is assumed; G2 prevents turning raw modeled IAS3.45 into a ranked investment conclusion.

Model correction, 20 October 2026: this changes our cash-flow/terminal-claim treatment, not the issuer’s reported history. The prior conditional tax/statutory payment already settled ₹7.88 crore tax less75% of ₹7.75 crore unallocated government assets, plus ₹4.03 crore statutory dues. This is still a conditional credit assumption, not proof those government balances are income-tax credits. A new zero-credit bound pays the full tax/statutory claim, without recovering those assets elsewhere. Add ₹0.24 crore current gratuity/leave provisions once; keep salary, sitting fees and expense accruals ₹2.19 crore as a constant ordinary WC stock, separately stressed for accelerated payment. Retain ₹1.24 crore noncurrent employee provisions at terminal. Corrected linked scenarios: Base: illustrative terminal price ₹428.74; peak funding gap ₹0.0000 crore; conditional IRR 7.91%. Bull: illustrative terminal price ₹685.51; peak funding gap ₹0.0000 crore; conditional IRR 18.53%. Bear: illustrative terminal price ₹55.00; peak funding gap ₹34.0385 crore; no investable IRR. [A26]

sections.title: Bear Case and Permanent-Loss Analysis
sections.text: The bear path loses 30% first-year revenue, followed by 0/3/5/5% growth,10% EBITDA margin,90 extra collection days,10% opening-receivable impairment,15% net-inventory impairment,₹2.6014 bank-guarantee call sensitivity,15% factory overrun and 12% interest. These are distinct analyst stresses, not observed defaults, claims or write-offs. Charging losses as cash-equivalent reserve drains is deliberately conservative rather than a forecast tax-accounting entry. It produces a peak ₹34.04 crore gap to the ₹2 crore reserve and an unfunded no-rescue terminal illustration near ₹55.00 per share. Even releasing all ₹25.15 crore excluded deposits would not by itself close that peak gap, before obligations attached to their release. The≈−28.44% annualized terminal illustration is not a feasible financed shareholder return. Customer loss and working-capital delay can arrive together; capacity spend does not protect collections. D2 reflects credible severe permanent-loss/funding sensitivity despite a funded base and IPO cushion. No current default is asserted, and G3 is conditional rather than an observed failure.

sections.title: Fivefold and Tenfold Compounding Tests
sections.text: At unchanged 16318000 shares,5 x/10 x current market value require ₹2390.59/4781.17 crore equity value. At an illustrative 20 x sustainable PAT, that needs ₹119.53/239.06 crore profit, compared with ₹22.93 reported and ₹19.54–21.81 normalized. At 14% PAT margin, implied revenue is about ₹853.78/1707.56 crore, before dilution or additional capital requirements. Management’s 4–5 x physical capacity claim is neither that profit outcome nor assured utilization. Even the selected bull terminal ₹685.51 is only 2.34 x entry over five years. A much longer horizon could change the arithmetic, but no reliable probability for 5 x/10 x is supported. Orders, skills, collection capital and returns on the full new facility must scale together.

sections.title: Monitoring Triggers and Thesis Breakers
sections.text: Prioritize a reconciled FY2026 cash-flow/interest/tax bridge and confirmation status, followed by reviewed H1FY2027 balance sheet/CFO rather than preliminary sales alone. Track the receivable cohort from March, customer concentration and overdue aging, not just closing DSO distorted by seasonality. Verify actual remaining debt and IPO monitoring-account/project spends without counting historical cash twice. Compare factory partial commissioning at end-Q3 and full integration by March 2027 with original dates, costs and customer qualification. Check obsolete inventory provision adequacy, warranty cash claims, tax/ROC compounding outcomes and audit-trail remediation. Refresh ESM/ST/price-band/lot and quote depth before implementation. Favorable reassessment needs sustained cash conversion after supplier payments and returns on the new capital; an unexplained large receivable rollover, new funding gap or unapproved material allocation change would weaken the thesis.

sections.title: Classification and Completion Status
sections.text: Deep research complete for the available cutoff evidence, with explicit unresolved reliability and implementation constraints. Classification: conditional growth watchlist/special situation, not a verified high-quality compounder, not a buy-ready ranking and not an accusation of misconduct. BQS5.40; Growth Quality 5.00 after cap; IAS NS under G2. All factor estimates and scenario arithmetic remain inspectable, with Medium evidence confidence rather than unsupported certainty. Research completion means a complete evidence-led assessment and a clear gate decision, not that every company passes diligence or every missing disclosure has been supplied.

sections.title: Sources, Scope and Reproduction
sections.text: Primary annual reports, final prospectus, corrected exchange results, monitoring report, management communications, AGM voting results and official NSE market/surveillance files underpin this review. Original, restated and regrouped series are separately labeled. Official 60-session turnover uses every observed session July 24–October 19, after the verified April 30 listing; no prelisting or missing-day zero imputation. October 19 REG1 is forward-effective October 21, not retroactive. Historical quality, forecast assumptions, calculations and outstanding questions are separated throughout. Source identifiers link to exact documents below; model and score-audit fields reproduce assumptions and arithmetic. No live executable bid/spread, current September 30 pledge filing or final compounding order was verified.

model_correction_2026_10_20.terminal_policy: Opening noncurrent employee/deposit claim retained at terminal, not assumed immediately due. Future operating margins include new employee costs; no extra growth in old provision or asset recovery is credited.

model_correction_2026_10_20.ordinary_stock_policy: The identified ordinary operating payable stock is held constant in nominal rupees in the reference opening and every forecast closing balance. The stated incremental WC forecast is after this constant stock; accelerated-settlement sensitivity reduces the stock to zero once and never charges it again.
